text.p: Following is a factfile on Switzerland's Martina Hingis, who became the youngest Grand Slam champion in modern tennis history on Saturday:
Born: Kosice, Slovakia, September 30, 1980, named after Czechoslovak tennis great Martina Navratilova
Aged two: Learns to walk and has tennis racquet put in her hand by mother Melanie, a former Czechoslovak champion who becomes her coach and driving force
Aged five: Played first competitive tennis
Aged seven: Left Czechoslovakia with her mother for new life in Switzerland
Aged 12: Became youngest junior champion at French Open, replacing previous record-holder Jennifer Capriati
Aged 13: Became youngest junior champion at Wimbledon
Aged 14: Made professional debut in Zurich, beating Patty Fendick 6-4 6-3 to become youngest player to win a singles match since tennis became open to professionals in 1968. Broke into top 20.
Aged 15: Became youngest ever champion at Grand Slam event when she won the women's doubles at Wimbledon with Helena Sukova of the Czech Republic.

Aged 16: Broke into top 10 a week after 16th birthday and took first tour title a week later. Beat former number one Monica Seles 6-2 6-0 in the final at Oakland tournament -- the worst defeat of Seles' career. Became the youngest player, male or female, to pass US$1 million of earnings in a season. Signed $10 million five-year endorsement deal with Italian sportswear label. Became youngest Australian Open champion in women's doubles and youngest Grand Slam singles champion, beating Mary Pierce of France.
Only Lottie Dod, who won Wimbledon in 1887 at the age of 15 years and 10 months, has won a major title at an earlier age -- but that was before Grand Slams were invented.
